issue: Is a second-in-time habeas petition that challenges an undisturbed conviction, filed after the prisoner obtained relief only as to his sentence, barred as second or successive under AEDPA?

sides.position: A second-in-time petition challenging an undisturbed conviction is barred as second or successive after the prisoner has already litigated a habeas petition, even if he obtained resentencing relief.
cases: Suggs v. United States, 705 F.3d 279 (7th Cir. 2013)

sides.position: A prisoner who receives relief as to his sentence is not barred from raising, in a second-in-time petition, a challenge to an undisturbed conviction, because a new judgment resets the count under Magwood.
cases: Lesko v. Secretary Pennsylvania Department of Corrections, 34 F.4th 211 (3d Cir. 2022)

this_court: A prisoner who receives relief as to his sentence is not barred from raising, in a second-in-time habeas petition, a challenge to an undisturbed conviction.
quote: the Seventh Circuit has adhered to its precedent and held that a second-in-time habeas petition is barred as second or successive where it attempts to challenge a prisoner's undisturbed conviction after he already litigated a habeas petition.
cite: John Lesko v. Secretary Pennsylvania Departm, 34 F.4th 211 (3rd Cir. 2022)
